The broader shared active-economy invariant still has the two concrete failures below.

S1 — MATERIAL (P2): packages/core/src/state/flexibleCasting.ts:189 (related :128-140, :153, :199-213; boundedProcedures.ts:1460-1520). Evaluation uses the Font of Magic procedure's duplicated maximum while mutation uses the active class table's maximum, without reconciling or rejecting disagreement. A stable, supported class-only add-on overrides the level-3 sorcerer's sorceryPoints capacity to 2; the inherited procedure still contains maximum 3. Through registered tools, spend_usage uses=1 correctly leaves 1/2 points. flexible_casting convert-slot slotLevel=2 then succeeds, consumes a level-2 slot, reports pointDelta=2, and persists remaining=2/max=2: the actual gain was only 1, silently clamped by restoreUsage. No resolver drift, malformed counter, or direct database resource mutation is required. Sibling variation: a class-only maximum 4 refuses create-slot at full points (cost 2) with "currentPoints exceeds ... maximum 3", and refuses converting level 2 after spending 2 points, although the active table permits both. Existing add-on tests update class and feature maxima together, so they cannot distinguish this failure. Authority: owning bead's exact slot-to-point conversion and point ceiling; SRD Font of Magic explicitly refers to the Sorcerer table; docs/design/character-progression.md selects table-derived Sorcery Points capacity; prior S2 requires evaluation and mutation to share one economy; ADR 0020 requires deterministic resource accounting. Suggested fix (owner: Flexible Casting/usage integration): use one authoritative active maximum for evaluation and mutation, or explicitly reject an inconsistent class/procedure binding atomically before consuming a slot; never let a successful conversion truncate the declared point gain. Permanent evidence: generalized invariant that every successful conversion's persisted point change equals pointDelta under independently varied class/feature maxima, with refused operations preserving all state. Cover create/convert, class-only and feature-only overrides, and absent/existing/alias counters. Small in-memory boundary tests are proportionate to the risk of losing a real slot for a misreported gain.

S2 — MATERIAL (P2): packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:1749 and :1763 (affected changed contract at :945-949; consumers state/rest.ts:703-709 and orchestrator/toolResetUsage.ts:69-79). The active-capacity repair reaches spend_usage and restore_usage, but resetUsage still selects, resets and reports the stored economy without active class reconciliation. Concrete scenario reproduced through complete_long_rest: spend one sorcery point for a level-3 sorcerer under bundled maximum 3, then bind a stable, internally consistent class + Font of Magic add-on with maximum 2. The long rest succeeds and returns usageReset with usesMax=3/usesRemaining=3; the canonical durable row remains uses_max=3/uses_used=0, although the bound maximum is 2. A matching maximum 4 still reports/persists 3 instead of 4. Sibling probes through reset_usage show the same stale maximum for Ki and Rage, for active maxima 2 and 4. This is also the compatibility state produced by the previous bundled-capacity resolver. A later spend repairs it, but does not correct the already persisted and model-visible rest result. Authority: owning bead's long-rest point recovery, prior shared active-capacity finding, docs/design/character-progression.md explicitly names reset_usage as a consumer of selected pack-bound capacities, and ADR 0020 state integrity. Suggested fix (owner: usage reset/rest integration): resolve the active rules stack once for the reset, reconcile selected class-resource counters within the event's actual owner/party scope before filtering by reset kind and returning results, and thread the resolver from reset_usage and rest callers. Reuse canonical alias adoption and preserve item/combatant and event semantics; handle missing/unavailable/none/unlimited capacities explicitly. Permanent evidence: generalized invariant that reset_usage and actual rest recovery persist/report the active maximum/reset/source for stale canonical and alias selected-resource counters, varying higher/lower capacities and owner scopes. This protects the same durable economy as the restore tests with proportionate in-memory evidence.

Verification: 11 targeted files passed, 310 tests (flexibleCasting, spellSlots, usageCounters, rest, spellUpcast, contextAssembler, contextAssemblerParty, tools, persistence, migrationLegacyAdoption, migrationRunner). Six targeted levelUpEngine resource/legacy tests and one source-derived Font of Magic evaluator test passed; other tests in those two files were excluded by name filters. Thirteen additional independent in-memory tool scenarios passed, covering resolver-call count and atomic refusal, duplicate-alias restoration for Sorcery Points/Ki/Rage, none/unlimited restoration, missing-slot rollback, created level-5 upcasting at sorcerer level 7, context visibility, short-rest preservation, and actual long-rest expiry/point recovery. Three independent class-only override probes reproduced S1; six consistent-override reset/rest probes reproduced S2. Used existing parent-resolved dependencies with native Vitest config loading and cache disabled. All probes ran from stdin and created no repository files. git diff --check passed; final worktree status clean at the assigned SHA. No install/build/format/verify, repository edits, GitHub writes, commits, pushes or merges.

No non-material findings recorded. Automatic bonus-action consumption has no requirement in this PR: the dispatch explicitly assigns it to the DM/existing turn-resource tool. Required next state: repair S1/S2 and review the resulting exact head before merge. The shared active-capacity defect class has survived two repair cycles; apply the review policy's churn rule and review the affected subsystem afresh rather than dispatch a third narrow example-only repair.

VERDICT: MATERIAL FINDINGS (2)
